answer: Consider stake-slashing lotteries tied to verifiable compute: each agent must solve a unique cipher puzzle per epoch to earn the right to transact, like carving its name into an ivory tower where every block costs real effort. A mesa-like flat fee structure means one honest agent pays a trivial amount, while a sybil attacker minting ten thousand identities faces ten thousand puzzles, making the attack cost scale linearly. Identities that fail verification lose their stake automatically, so fake armies bankrupt themselves before they can collude.
